evidence.note: Lists access tokens, authentication passwords and encryption keys among data that should not be recorded directly in logs.
secrecy crate exists to 'prevent accidental leakage of secrets via channels like debug logging'; its SecretBox Debug impl redacts.

rs-debug-derive-secret.whyNotLinter: Clippy has no secret-aware lint (only `missing_fields_in_debug` for manual impls). Recognizing that a field holds a secret takes judgment about its name and type.
rs-debug-derive-secret.aiRelevance: High. Agents add `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]` to every struct by reflex, including config and credential structs.
rs-debug-derive-secret.expectedNoise: low — both the field names and the derive are visible in the snippet.
rs-debug-derive-secret.evidenceStatus: single official B source for the exact API; needs a second B (or A from a repo) before shipping as built-in, or accept it on the strength of the vendor doc

evidence.note: Primary defense: prepared statements with parameterized queries (standard reference, not re-fetched).

rs-sql-built-with-format.whyNotLinter: Clippy has no SQL lint, and the compiler can't tell SQL text from other strings. Telling identifiers from an allowlist apart from user values takes judgment.
rs-sql-built-with-format.aiRelevance: Medium-high. Agents use `format!` for dynamic filters and `IN (...)` lists when the bind syntax for the driver is unfamiliar.
rs-sql-built-with-format.expectedNoise: low — allowlisted identifiers are the only common look-alike, and they're a listed negative.

evidence.note: Separate arguments are passed literally rather than through shell syntax; Windows special decoders require separate care.
Externally influenced data in OS command syntax can allow an attacker to modify the intended command.

rs-shell-command-interpolation.whyNotLinter: Requires distinguishing shell syntax from literal args, quoting and allowlisted input; Command use alone is not a defect.
rs-shell-command-interpolation.aiRelevance: External input interpreted by a shell can run unintended commands.
rs-shell-command-interpolation.expectedNoise: Low with explicit shell invocation and externally supplied text.
rs-shell-command-interpolation.versions: Tokio 1.54.1, reqwest 0.13.5 and current stable Rust/zip docs where applicable; APIs also exist in earlier supported releases.

evidence.note: enclosed_name rejects null bytes, absolute paths and paths resolving outside the current directory.
Unrestricted path components and absolute paths can escape an intended directory.

rs-zip-entry-path-traversal.whyNotLinter: Requires connecting an archive-provided name to a write destination and recognizing validation; listing an entry name is safe.
rs-zip-entry-path-traversal.aiRelevance: Untrusted archive entries can overwrite files outside the extraction root.
rs-zip-entry-path-traversal.expectedNoise: Low for direct joins; does not claim symlink or race protection.
rs-zip-entry-path-traversal.versions: Tokio 1.54.1, reqwest 0.13.5 and current stable Rust/zip docs where applicable; APIs also exist in earlier supported releases.

evidence.note: Path::starts_with compares whole path components, unlike a string prefix.
Traversal and inadequate pathname validation can bypass restrictions to an intended directory.

rs-path-string-prefix-containment.whyNotLinter: Requires recognizing filesystem authorization rather than ordinary naming or URL checks and checking canonicalization/boundaries.
rs-path-string-prefix-containment.aiRelevance: A sibling directory can pass a textual prefix authorization check.
rs-path-string-prefix-containment.expectedNoise: Low to medium: canonical separator-terminated strings are explicitly exempt.
rs-path-string-prefix-containment.versions: Tokio 1.54.1, reqwest 0.13.5 and current stable Rust/zip docs where applicable; APIs also exist in earlier supported releases.
